Only 22% of remote job listings state a pay figure. The other 78% are marked DOE — determined on experience — leaving you to guess the USD salary you are worth.

According to Loker Dollar's data on 4,280 active remote listings, just 940 (22%) disclose a concrete USD salary. The remaining 3,340 leave pay blank, effectively a DOE arrangement.

DOE is a negotiation lever, not necessarily a red flag. Employers keep budgets flexible and tailor pay to seniority, which can work in your favor if you have rare, in-demand skills. One real example: Online Consumer Panels America lists $25–$45/hour for product assessments.

How to handle a DOE listing:
• Research global benchmarks for your role
• Quantify your impact with concrete metrics
• Anchor high with a range, then let the employer adjust
• Ask about total compensation (benefits, equity, bonuses)

Of the 4,280 listings, 2,735 (64%) accept applicants from any country — and 1,213 were posted in the last 7 days. For Indonesians chasing remote USD roles, that is a wide open field.

Read the full breakdown here:
